body:
Myk's ruling (2026-08-25): the accessibility law outranks the terms-budget count.
"Checkpoint" is load-bearing from lesson 5 and gets its glossary entry.

BUILD AFTER #465 (the §48 landing) merges. The frozen-rail choreography is the whole trick:
test/site/arc.test.ts is FROZEN (archived T227's rail) and pins the terms manifest against a
hand-written list — adding a 22nd term reds it. So this is the two-PR rail-renames discipline:
(1) the authorization PR lands the single-line pairs in scripts/rail-renames.json (the count
line and the list line — pairs are single-line printable-ASCII; verify the exact frozen lines
first and write pairs that leave base+substitution byte-identical), Myk merges it per the
mechanism; (2) the build PR adds the term to lessons.mjs (lesson 5 plants the glossary delta
with a plain-words definition: "a saved copy of your whole diary at a lesson's end, so you can
come back"), the manifest, and the scan expectations via the authorized substitution.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) Lesson 5 introduces "checkpoint" in plain words before its first bare use, plants the
    glossary delta, and the vocabulary scan passes with 22 terms. Verify: the (authorized)
    arc.test.ts run plus the browser glossary case.
(b) The rename pairs are spent and removed in the follow-up per the discipline. Verify:
    rail-renames.json empty of these pairs after both PRs land.

Merge tier: the authorization PR is Myk's by mechanism; the build PR self-merges on green.
title: "checkpoint" becomes the 22nd glossary term (after #465 merges)
